advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether _code_review_prompt_id should tolerate an unresolvable/malformed criteria overlay (mirroring _criterion_id's try/except) or intentionally propagate, and make the two arms consistent.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:201-208: `if repo_root is not None:` ... `valid |= {criterion_prompt_id(...) for criterion_id in effective_criteria(repo_root)}` (no guard)
src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:73-76: `_criterion_id` wraps `registry.by_id(repo_root)` in `try: ... except Exception: return None  # registry unresolvable ⇒ treat as non-criterion`
src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py:288-291: effective_criteria raises `CriteriaError(... 'activate' must be a list of ids ...)` on a malformed overlay
advisory.finding: _code_review_prompt_id() calls effective_criteria(repo_root) without a try/except, so a malformed `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay raises CriteriaError and propagates out of run_case for any prompt_id starting with `code-review-`. The sibling _criterion_id() (invoked earlier in run_case with the same repo_root) intentionally swallows registry-resolution failures and returns None, so the same malformed overlay silently skips the plan-review criterion arm but then hard-errors at the code-review check — an inconsistent, surprising failure mode.
scenarios: A repo with a malformed/invalid `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` overlay runs an eval on any code-review prompt id
calibrate_criterion or run_case invoked for a `code-review-*` prompt in such a repo

scenarios: A maintainer reads the docstring to understand what ids this arm accepts
